entries.name: BleedingTooth — A2MP Heap Type Confusion
entries.description: A heap-based type confusion in process_l2cap_cmd() for A2MP CID 0x0003 allows an attacker in Bluetooth range to escalate privileges or execute code in kernel context.

entries.name: BleedingTooth — A2MP Info Leak
entries.description: Improper access control in process_l2cap_cmd() leaks kernel stack memory via A2MP GetInfo response, useful for KASLR bypass.

entries.name: BIAS — Bluetooth Impersonation Attack
entries.description: Authentication procedure in Bluetooth Classic allows impersonation of a previously paired device without knowing the link key, by downgrading to legacy auth.

entries.name: KNOB — Key Negotiation of Bluetooth
entries.description: The encryption key length negotiation in Bluetooth BR/EDR can be forced to 1 byte by an active MitM attacker, enabling brute-force of the session key.

entries.name: BLUFFS — Bluetooth Forward & Future Secrecy
entries.description: Multiple attacks against Bluetooth session key derivation break forward and future secrecy across sessions, enabling MitM and session decryption.

entries.name: Android BLE use-after-free (l2cap_reassemble_sdu)
entries.description: Use-after-free in l2cap_reassemble_sdu() in the Android kernel Bluetooth stack allows an attacker in Bluetooth range to execute code in kernel context.

entries.name: BleedingBit — ESP32 BLE OOB Write
entries.description: Out-of-bounds write in Espressif's BLE stack via malformed L2CAP packet, allowing code execution on the ESP32 MCU.

entries.name: Zephyr BLE HCI buffer overflow
entries.description: Buffer overflow in Zephyr RTOS HCI layer via crafted BLE advertisement. Allows memory corruption on Zephyr-based BLE devices.

entries.name: BlueZ sdptool arbitrary command injection
entries.description: BlueZ sdptool contains a command injection vulnerability. Not directly remotely exploitable but relevant in post-exploitation or toolchain context.

entries.name: runc container escape via /proc/self/exe
entries.description: runc allows a malicious container to overwrite the host runc binary via /proc/self/exe, enabling host escape with root privileges.

entries.name: BlueZ heap out-of-bounds read in L2CAP
entries.description: Out-of-bounds read in BlueZ L2CAP leads to information disclosure. May expose kernel addresses for KASLR bypass.

entries.name: BlueZ gatt-database use-after-free
entries.description: Use-after-free in BlueZ GATT database triggered by a BLE peer disconnecting during service enumeration.

entries.name: BlueZ A2DP heap-based buffer overflow
entries.description: Heap-based buffer overflow in BlueZ A2DP profile via a malformed A2MP command, exploitable without authentication.

entries.name: BlueZ incomplete D-Bus authorization
entries.description: Incomplete authorization check in BlueZ D-Bus interface allows local users to pair devices or access sensitive operations without proper permissions.

entries.name: BlueDucky — HID injection via unauthenticated BLE pairing
entries.description: An unauthenticated BLE device can pair as an HID keyboard without confirmation and inject keystrokes to the victim device.

entries.name: SweynTooth — BLE Link Layer length overflow family
entries.affected_component: Multiple BLE SoC SDKs (nRF5, TI CC26x2, Cypress, Dialog)
entries.description: A family of BLE Link Layer vulnerabilities in major SoC SDKs, including length overflow and invalid length fields causing crashes or bypassing pairing.

entries.name: BLURtooth — CTKD key overwrite
entries.description: CTKD allows overwriting existing pairing keys during dual-mode connection, enabling impersonation of already-paired devices.

entries.name: Linux mm use-after-free (anon VMA)
entries.description: Use-after-free in Linux kernel mm subsystem. Combined with IoT devices having local unprivileged user, can be chained for LPE.

entries.name: Sequoia — Linux filesystem size_t-to-int overflow
entries.description: size_t-to-int conversion overflow in seq_file allows unprivileged local users to write out-of-bounds to kernel memory, achieving root.

entries.name: PwnKit — pkexec local privilege escalation
entries.description: Out-of-bounds write in pkexec argv[0] handling allows any local user to escalate to root.

entries.name: polkit D-Bus authentication bypass
entries.description: Race condition in polkit D-Bus message handling allows any unprivileged user to create new privileged account without authentication.

entries.name: Dasan GPON home router command injection
entries.description: Unauthenticated command injection in Dasan GPON router diagnostic endpoint. Common in industrial IoT gateways repackaging similar firmware.

entries.name: Wirepas Mesh SDK outdated dependency RCE
entries.description: Wirepas Gateway Python SDK ships with outdated protobuf dependency vulnerable to deserialization RCE. Exploitable via gRPC endpoint.

entries.name: Chromium V8 type confusion
entries.description: Included for reference — IoT devices with embedded browsers (dashboards) may expose this.

entries.name: Eclipse Kura command injection
entries.description: Eclipse Kura IoT framework exposes a REST endpoint /kura/rest/v1/services/command that executes arbitrary shell commands when authenticated with default admin/admin credentials.

entries.name: Mosquitto MQTT broker DoS
entries.description: Malformed SUBSCRIBE packet causes Mosquitto to crash, resulting in denial of service for all connected IoT devices.

entries.name: Linux SCSI target information disclosure / RCE
entries.description: Improper handling in Linux SCSI target subsystem. Relevant for IoT devices with iSCSI storage. Can lead to arbitrary read/write of kernel memory.

entries.name: Linux netfilter heap out-of-bounds write
entries.description: Heap out-of-bounds write in Linux netfilter via XT_ALIGN. Local LPE to root; useful in post-exploitation after initial access on IoT.

entries.name: SSID confusion attack (WiFi IEEE 802.11)
entries.description: Design flaw in 802.11 allows connecting a client to a wrong network by using same BSSID and credentials. Affects IoT gateways with WiFi management.

entries.name: Linux USB gadget UAF in configfs
entries.description: Use-after-free in USB gadget configfs. On IoT devices where attacker can connect USB peripheral, enables LPE.

entries.name: BLE improper access control in pairing
entries.description: Improper access control during Bluetooth pairing allows an unauthenticated attacker to bypass authentication for previously bonded devices.

entries.name: URGENT/11 — VxWorks IPnet TCP Urgent Pointer OOB Read
entries.affected_component: Wind River VxWorks IPnet TCP/IP stack
entries.description: One of 11 URGENT/11 vulnerabilities in VxWorks IPnet stack. Heap overflow via TCP urgent pointer allows unauthenticated RCE. Affects industrial controllers, medical devices, SCADA.

entries.name: URGENT/11 — VxWorks IPnet IPv4 Options Stack Overflow
entries.description: Stack overflow in IPv4 options parsing in VxWorks IPnet. Unauthenticated remote code execution via crafted IP packet.

entries.name: FreeRTOS+TCP Heap Overflow (multiple)
entries.description: Multiple heap and stack overflow vulnerabilities in FreeRTOS+TCP. Crafted TCP/IP packets trigger buffer overflows allowing unauthenticated RCE on embedded devices running FreeRTOS.

entries.name: Zephyr USB DFU Class Buffer Overflow
entries.description: Buffer overflow in Zephyr USB Device Firmware Upgrade class. Attacker with physical USB access can overwrite memory and execute arbitrary code.

entries.name: Zephyr Shell Stack Overflow
entries.description: Stack-based buffer overflow in Zephyr shell via overly long command string. Accessible over BLE or UART shell interface.

entries.name: U-Boot i2c buffer overflow
entries.description: Buffer overflow in U-Boot i2c subsystem allows arbitrary code execution during boot. Exploitable via malicious TFTP image or local console.

entries.name: U-Boot TFTP buffer overflow
entries.description: Buffer overflow in U-Boot TFTP client when processing large UDP fragmented packets. Exploitable from local network during PXE/TFTP boot.

entries.name: Contiki-NG Buffer Overflow in 6LoWPAN
entries.description: Buffer overflow in Contiki-NG 6LoWPAN fragmentation reassembly. Crafted 802.15.4 packets cause heap overflow, enabling code execution on embedded nodes.

entries.name: Contiki-NG Out-of-Bounds Read in MQTT
entries.description: Out-of-bounds read in Contiki-NG MQTT client allows a malicious broker to crash IoT nodes or leak memory contents.

entries.name: ThreadX / NetX Duo TCP/IP Stack Overflow
entries.description: Multiple integer overflows and buffer overflows in Azure RTOS NetX Duo TCP/IP stack. Unauthenticated RCE via crafted network packets on embedded devices running ThreadX.

entries.name: mbed TLS Heap Buffer Overflow in Certificate Parsing
entries.description: Heap buffer overflow in Mbed TLS X.509 certificate parser. Malformed certificate triggers overflow, potential RCE on embedded TLS clients.

entries.name: OPC UA .NET Stack infinite loop DoS
entries.description: Infinite loop in OPC UA .NET stack certificate validation. Relevant for industrial IoT gateways exposing OPC UA (port 4840).

entries.name: sudo privilege escalation via sudoedit
entries.description: sudo sudoedit allows privilege escalation via EDITOR variable manipulation. Common on embedded Linux gateways where sudo is present.

entries.name: BLE Mesh Provisioning — Impersonation Attack
entries.description: An attacker within range of a provisioner and a device being provisioned can impersonate the device and complete the exchange, obtaining the NetKey. Requires the AuthValue to be known, guessable, or absent (the No OOB method), which is the common default in shipped products.

entries.name: BLE Mesh Provisioning — AuthValue Leak
entries.description: A device being provisioned can leak the AuthValue to an attacker who initiates provisioning before the legitimate provisioner. Once the AuthValue is known the attacker completes the exchange and receives the NetKey.

entries.name: BLE Mesh Provisioning — Predictable AuthValue
entries.description: Implementations that use a fixed or predictable AuthValue let an attacker brute-force it offline from a captured Provisioning Confirmation PDU, then complete provisioning as a legitimate party and obtain the NetKey. Short Output/Input OOB sizes make the search space trivially small.

entries.name: BLE Mesh Provisioning — Malleable Commitment
entries.description: The provisioning commitment is malleable: an attacker can craft alternate values that satisfy the confirmation check, letting them complete provisioning without knowing the AuthValue and obtain the NetKey.

entries.name: Passkey Entry Impersonation (LE Secure Connections and Mesh)
entries.affected_component: Bluetooth LE Secure Connections / Mesh provisioning Passkey Entry
entries.affected_versions: Bluetooth Core 2.1 through 5.2, Mesh Profile 1.0 and 1.0.1
entries.description: In Passkey Entry pairing, a machine-in-the-middle can learn the passkey one bit per round by reflecting the peer's public key, then complete authenticated pairing or provisioning while impersonating both sides.
detection_hints: Input OOB or Output OOB authentication in use

entries.name: BR/EDR PIN Pairing Impersonation
entries.description: An attacker can spoof the BD_ADDR of a peer and complete legacy PIN pairing without knowing the PIN, establishing an authenticated link key with the victim. Relevant to gateways that keep BR/EDR enabled alongside BLE Mesh.

entries.name: Zephyr BLE Mesh — Provisioning PDU Length Buffer Overflow
entries.description: Improper handling of the length field of an incoming Bluetooth Mesh provisioning PDU allows an unauthenticated attacker in range to overflow a buffer, causing memory corruption and potentially code execution on the node.

entries.name: Zephyr BLE Mesh — Provisioning Link Assertion (DoS)
entries.description: Repeatedly opening a Bluetooth Mesh provisioning link reaches an assertion in the provisioning state machine and halts the node. An attacker in range can keep a node permanently offline without any key material.

entries.name: Directed Forwarding routing manipulation (research, no CVE assigned)
entries.affected_versions: Mesh Protocol 1.1 implementations with Directed Forwarding enabled
entries.description: Directed Forwarding replaces managed flooding with explicit paths built by a path-discovery exchange. That exchange creates routing state other nodes can influence. A party holding a valid NetKey - including a compromised, salvaged or resold node - can inject path control messages so it becomes the forwarder for a chosen destination and then discard that traffic, producing targeted denial of service and topology manipulation that managed flooding has no equivalent state for. Published as 'Tous les chemins menent a DROP' at SSTIC 2025 by Tali, Cayre, Nicomette and Auriol (LAAS-CNRS).
